1.

2. The present application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.181 of 2023 under sections 376, 313, 506 I.P.C., Police Station P.G.I., District Lucknow.

3. In pursuance of the earlier order, informant/victim of the case is present and she categorically stated that she does not want to prosecute the applicant and she has no objection, in case,

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that as per the prosecution case, victim of the case is aged about 31 years, she is also working as a teacher and on the pretext of marriage, applicant made physical relation with her and when she conceived then the fetus was aborted forcibly, then F.I.R. in question was lodged.

He further submitted that victim of the present case is also a teacher in the Central School, Memaura, Lucknow and she herself admitted in the F.I.R. that she is in relation with the applicant and a divorcee.
He further submitted that applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation and he does not have any criminal antecedent, therefore, he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer of the applicant and submitted that allegations of rape has been alleged in the F.I.R. but he does not dispute this fact that victim who is aged about 31 years,
working as a teacher in the Central School alongwith the applicant.

He also does not dispute this fact that compromise deed is filed by the victim of the present case and stated she does not want to prosecute the applicant and the issue in question has been settled out of the Court.
6. Learned counsel for the complainant submitted that she has no objection, in case anticipatory bail is granted to the applicant.

7. Considering the argument of learned counsel for the parties and going through the contents of the FIR, statement of the victim, compromise deed as well as other relevant documents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.
8. Thus having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is finally disposed of.

In case, applicant- Krishan Kumar, involved in aforesaid case crime number is taken into custody, he shall be released on anticipatory bail by the concerned Station House Officer on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount with the following conditions:-
i.
The applicant shall not leave India during the pendency of trial without prior permission from the concerned trial Court.
ii. The applicant shall Cooperate in the investigation and will make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
iii. The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.
iv. The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of any of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law to ensure presence of the applicant.
